post.caption: Only a diamond can polish a diamond. Diamond is the hardest natural material, ranking 10 on the Mohs scale, so polishers grind with dust made from other diamonds. The dust is mixed with olive oil and goes onto a spinning cast iron wheel called a scaife. Cutters must work with the grain, because some directions barely polish. To shape a stone's outline, two diamonds are rubbed together, and the dust that rubs off is collected and put to use. Tradition credits Lodewyk van Bercken of Bruges with the scaife in 1476, though some historians doubt it. A round brilliant has 57 or 58 facets, depending on the culet.
